title: Private Markets and Private Credit for Managers
summary: An eight-module advanced programme giving private markets managers and service providers the tools to manage valuation, leverage, liquidity and conflicts risks and meet supervisory expectations.
intro: This training programme equips private markets managers and their service providers to manage the structural, valuation, leverage, liquidity and conflicts risks of private equity, private credit and semi-liquid funds, and to meet rising supervisory expectations.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give managers and service providers in private markets an advanced, practical understanding of where risk and conflicts concentrate as the asset class grows and opens to wider investors. Participants leave able to strengthen valuation, liquidity, leverage and conflicts controls, and see their business the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: Private markets structures and strategies, fund finance and leverage including subscription lines and NAV facilities, valuation, liquidity in semi-liquid and evergreen vehicles, conflicts in continuation vehicles and co-investment, fees, disclosure and investor reporting, retail access and distribution, and risk management and supervisory focus.
Intended Audience: Senior managers, investment professionals and partners at private equity, private credit and real assets managers
Compliance, risk, valuation, finance and investor relations teams at private markets managers
Fund administrators, depositaries, auditors, lenders and distributors servicing private markets funds
Learning Objectives: Explain how private markets structures and strategies create distinct risks for managers and investors
Evaluate the use of fund finance and leverage at fund and portfolio level
Design robust valuation governance for illiquid and stressed assets
Apply liquidity management to semi-liquid and evergreen vehicles
Manage conflicts, fees and disclosure in line with investor and supervisory expectations
Strengthen risk management, retail distribution controls and readiness for supervisory scrutiny
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, valuation and liquidity exercises and practical templates, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's strategies and investor base.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of private markets, fund management or fund servicing is helpful. No prior knowledge of specific fund rules is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Thematic Analysis: Emerging Risks in Private Finance (2023)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)
FSB, Global Monitoring Report on Non-Bank Financial Intermediation (annual)

modules.title: Private Markets Structures and Strategies
modules.summary: The main private markets strategies and fund structures, how their economics work, and why growth and wider investor access are drawing supervisory attention.
objectives: Distinguish private equity, private credit, real assets and secondaries strategies
Explain closed-ended, evergreen and semi-liquid fund structures
Identify the risks that arise from the private markets business model
syllabus: Buyout, growth, direct lending, asset-based finance, infrastructure and real estate
Limited partnerships, feeders, parallel funds and evergreen vehicles
Capital calls, distributions, waterfalls and carried interest
Links between private markets, banks, insurers and pension funds

modules.title: Fund Finance and Leverage
modules.summary: How subscription lines, NAV facilities and portfolio-level leverage are used, their effect on returns and risk, and the controls and disclosures they require.
objectives: Explain how subscription lines and NAV facilities work
Assess the effect of fund finance on performance metrics and investor risk
Design leverage limits, monitoring and disclosure
syllabus: Subscription lines: uses, terms and effect on internal rates of return
NAV facilities, hybrid facilities and distributions funded by borrowing
Portfolio company leverage, payment-in-kind interest and covenant erosion
Leverage measurement, limits and investor disclosure

modules.title: Valuation of Private Assets
modules.summary: How private equity, private credit and real assets are valued, how valuation governance provides independence and challenge, and how uncertainty is handled under stress.
objectives: Apply market, income and cost approaches to private assets
Design valuation governance with functional independence and challenge
Address valuation uncertainty for stressed and amended positions
syllabus: Valuation approaches, inputs and the use of comparables
Valuation policies, committees, independent valuers and audit
Stressed loans, amendments, extensions and valuation lag
Case study: challenging a private credit portfolio valuation

modules.title: Liquidity in Semi-Liquid and Evergreen Vehicles
modules.summary: How semi-liquid and evergreen funds offer periodic liquidity on illiquid assets, the mismatch risks this creates, and the tools and stress testing needed to manage them.
objectives: Assess liquidity mismatch between assets, redemption terms and investor base
Design liquidity buffers, redemption limits and liquidity management tools
Stress test liquidity under adverse market and redemption scenarios
syllabus: Redemption frequency, notice periods, gates and lock-ups
Liquidity sleeves, credit facilities and secondary sales
Liquidity stress testing and early warning indicators
Fair treatment of redeeming and remaining investors

modules.title: Conflicts: Continuation Vehicles and Co-Investment
modules.summary: Where conflicts concentrate in private markets, including continuation vehicles, co-investment and cross-fund transactions, and how to identify, manage and evidence fair treatment.
objectives: Identify conflicts in manager-led secondaries and cross-fund transactions
Design fair co-investment and deal allocation policies
Use fairness opinions, advisory committees and disclosure effectively
syllabus: Continuation vehicles: pricing, process and investor elections
Co-investment rights, allocation policies and preferential terms
Cross-fund transactions, related-party services and affiliated lenders
Advisory committees, consents and conflicts registers

modules.title: Fees, Expenses, Disclosure and Investor Reporting
modules.summary: How fees and expenses are charged and allocated across funds and portfolio companies, and how to report performance, costs and risks transparently to investors.
objectives: Explain management fees, carried interest, offsets and portfolio-level fees
Allocate expenses fairly across funds, co-investors and the manager
Produce clear and comparable investor reporting on performance and costs
syllabus: Fee structures, offsets, monitoring fees and fund expenses
Expense allocation and broken-deal costs
Performance measures: IRR, multiples and the effect of fund finance
Quarterly reporting, capital account statements and side letter transparency

modules.title: Retail Access and Distribution
modules.summary: How private markets are being opened to wealth and retail investors through new vehicles and channels, and the product governance and disclosure controls this demands.
objectives: Assess the risks of offering private markets to wealth and retail investors
Design target market, suitability and distribution controls
Disclose fees, liquidity limits and valuation uncertainty clearly
syllabus: Wealth platforms, feeder funds, retirement savings and tokenised access
Product governance, target market and investor eligibility
Distributor oversight, marketing communications and investor understanding
Lessons from redemption pressure in semi-liquid funds

modules.title: Risk Management and Supervisory Focus
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around an integrated risk management framework, the issues supervisors are prioritising in private markets, and a practical readiness plan.
objectives: Build an integrated risk framework for credit, leverage, liquidity and operational risk
Anticipate supervisory priorities and international standard-setter work on private finance
Produce a supervisory readiness action plan
syllabus: Independent risk function, risk appetite and portfolio monitoring
Operational and third-party risk in fund administration and servicing
IOSCO and FSB work on private finance and non-bank leverage
Workshop: seeing the private markets business the way a supervisor does

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
related.summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
related.summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.
